'''Updating items''' refers to the tools [[Matcha Flavoured]] provides for bringing items from older versions of the pack up to date, chiefly the <code>/trigger update_item</code> command added in [[Matcha Flavoured 1.12.2|1.12.2]].

== Background ==
Datapacks cannot add items, so every custom item is a vanilla item with extra data components (name, model, lore, enchantments, attributes). An item keeps the components it was created with, so when a new version changes an item's stats, textures or name, old copies stay as they were and often no longer stack with new ones. In 1.12.2 almost all models and data moved from the <code>minecraft</code> and <code>main</code> namespaces to <code>matcha</code>, which made many old items appear broken.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.2|quote=So the previous models either minecraft:x or main:x have been moved to matcha:x}}</ref>

== /trigger update_item ==
Hold the item in the main hand and run <code>/trigger update_item</code>. Any player can use it without cheats.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/update_old_items/check_trigger.mcfunction}}</ref> The function:<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/update_old_items/update_held_item.mcfunction}}</ref>
# Reads the translation key of the held item's name. An item without one is rejected with "The held item cannot be updated because it is missing a translation key."
# Looks the key up in a table of 301 current item definitions, generated from the pack's crafting, smithing and food recipes and its villager trades. For 13 items whose only change is the item model ([[Amber]], [[Opal]], [[Ruby]], [[Topaz]], the [[Fox Pelt|fox pelt]], the clay statues ([[Clay Fetish (Rejoice)|cheerful]] and [[Clay Fetish (Lament)|mournful]]), [[Tallow|tallow]], the [[Ofuda|ofuda]], a recipe page, the classic porkchop and the two classic roses), a small item modifier is applied to the held stack instead, which sets the new model and leaves everything else alone.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/item_modifier/amber.json}}</ref> Items whose key is not in the table are reported as "The held item cannot be updated."
# Builds the current version of the item, and carries over the stack size and custom name. Durability damage is kept as a proportion of the new maximum.
# Merges the old item's enchantments, armor trim and lodestone compass target onto the new one; where both have an enchantment, the higher level is kept. Vanilla [[Fortune]] is then capped at level I, the pack's maximum.
# Removes the held item and drops the new one at the player's feet with no pickup delay, then reports "The held item has been successfully updated."

The table is generated by the script <code>generate_update_item_mcfunction.py</code> in the repository.<ref>{{Source|generate_update_item_mcfunction.py}}</ref>

=== Limitations ===
Only items whose name carries a translation key can be updated, so an item renamed with an anvil keeps its custom name but must still have the original key underneath. In 1.12.2 the function also looked items up by their item ID, which rebuilt any item on one of those vanilla IDs as the table entry (any splash potion became a [[Pickled Warped Fungus|pickled warped fungus]]), lost armor trims and lodestone compass targets, and had no entries for items only villagers sell. Since 1.12.3 the ID table is gone, villager-trade items are covered and trims and compass targets are kept.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/update_old_items/update_held_item.mcfunction}}</ref>

== Automatic updates ==
* Since 1.12.4, most of the pack's items update themselves. Whenever the player's inventory changes, an item in the main hand, the off hand or an armor slot that matches one of 421 pack items but lacks the current version tag (the custom data <code>version: 1</code>) has its components rewritten to the current definition. Items made in 1.12.4 carry the tag and are left alone.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha_item/advancement/trigger/chocolate.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha_item/item_modifier/modify/chocolate.json}}</ref><ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.4|quote=You won't need to trigger update any of the armour/tools, it will just work as soon as your inventory "changes" (picking up any item, moving any item around etc)}}</ref> The functions for enchanted equipment are also meant to raise its enchantments to at least the current levels, but they call functions under <code>matcha_item:enchants/</code>, which the pack doesn't have, so that step does nothing.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha_item/function/update/adamant_chestplate.mcfunction}}</ref> The files are generated by the script <code>generate_item_update_files.py</code> from <code>item_updater_db.json</code>.<ref>{{Source|generate_item_update_files.py}}</ref> The 26.3 port has none of this yet.
* The sacred texts (The Avesta, The Book of Enoch, The Divine Comedy, The Lesser Key of Solomon, Paradise Lost, The Quran and The Tanakh) and the "Golden" music disc are replaced automatically when picked up, outside Creative mode.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/update_old_items/quran.json}}</ref>
* Vanilla water bottles and unenchanted vanilla elytra are converted into the pack's versions.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/item_contingencies/elytra.mcfunction}}</ref> In 1.12.2 vanilla apples, sweet berries and turtle scutes were converted as well; the 1.12.3 pack no longer does this.
* When a player joins after an update, their recipe unlocks and most progression and reward [[advancements]] are reset, so that new recipes can unlock and rewards can be earned again. In 1.12.2 this included nearly the whole tutorial tab; 1.12.3 revokes a shorter list. See [[Advancements#Revocation on update]].

== Other methods ==
* <code>/loot give @s loot matcha:...</code> gives a fresh copy of many items, for example <code>matcha:treasure/divine_comedy</code>.
* For a sentimental item the trigger cannot rebuild, the 1.12.3 release notes suggest throwing it on the ground and running <code>/data merge entity @n[type=item] {Item:{components:{"item_model":"matcha:XXX"}}}</code>, where <code>XXX</code> is the item's model name from the English language file (for example <code>oarfish</code> or <code>mournful_clay_statue</code>).<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.3|quote=Replace the XXX with the item name}}</ref>
* Loading the previous resource pack below the new one hides broken textures, although enchantments stay broken.
* The weaponsmith (grindstone villager) melts alloyed equipment into its components, and an [[Amnestic|amnestic]] resets a villager's trades (after the 1.12.3 changes, villagers need one to unlock the new trades). Both were added in [[Matcha Flavoured 1.10|1.10]].
